items.title: Lillie Delk Christian Interview, 1961-04-25
items.q: And Tommy Christian. It was a band that was active in 1927

ctx.x: That might be his son, because he had two. One was playing trumpet, the other one was playing saxophone. His eldest son was playing the trumpet, I think, and his youngest son was playing the saxophone, I think. That you've made a song? Uh-huh. Yeah, that's all. I loved it.

You haven't in recent years? They're here? Yeah. No, I haven't. I haven't made any. Well, I hope that one of these times we'll have a chance to record you performing with a cheer club group. I'm going to see whether whoever would like to be recorded. Alphabetical. It isn't hard. There are several other Christian names here. They aren't related to Mr. Christian, are they? No. No. Of course you remember. I know that. Charlie Christian. Oh, I know that. Yes, I remember him. And Tommy Christian. It was a band that…
Uh-huh. Most of them... You know, so many musicians are from New Orleans.
